related_questions.question: How long can you live with pancreatic cancer?

text_blocks.snippet: The prognosis for pancreatic cancer varies significantly based on the stage at diagnosis and other individual factors, but overall, survival rates are relatively low. For localized cancer, the five-year survival rate is around 44%, while for distant (metastatic) cancer, it drops to 3%. The median survival time for untreated advanced pancreatic cancer is around 3.5 months, but with good treatment, this can extend to about eight months. Factors like tumor size, lymph node involvement, and degree of metastasis, as well as early diagnosis and treatment, play crucial roles in determining survival.

Median survival for advanced, untreated cancer: Around 3.5 months.
Early diagnosis and treatment: Crucial for better outcomes.
Tumor-specific treatment: Can significantly impact survival.
Age: Younger patients tend to have better outcomes.
Overall health and nutrition: Important for overall survival.

related_questions.question: What is the most common first symptom of pancreatic cancer?
related_questions.snippet: Most people with pancreatic cancer (and nearly all people with ampullary cancer) will have jaundice as one of their first symptoms. Jaundice is caused by the buildup of bilirubin, a dark yellow-brown substance made in the liver. Normally, the liver releases a liquid called bile that contains bilirubin.

related_questions.question: What are the four stages of pancreatic cancer?

text_blocks.snippet: Pancreatic cancer is staged from 0 to 4, with 0 being the earliest and 4 being the most advanced. The four stages are: Stage 0 (Carcinoma in situ), Stage I (localized to the pancreas), Stage II (spread to nearby tissues and lymph nodes), and Stage III (spread to major blood vessels or nerves near the pancreas). Stage IV is the most advanced stage, with distant metastasis.
snippet_highlighted_words: Stage 0 (Carcinoma in situ), Stage I (localized to the pancreas), Stage II (spread to nearby tissues and lymph nodes), and Stage III (spread to major blood vessels or nerves near the pancreas)

list.title: Stage 0 (Carcinoma in situ):
list.snippet: Cancer is only in the cells lining the pancreas and has not spread to deeper tissues.

list.title: Stage I:
list.snippet: Cancer is only in the pancreas. This stage is further divided into Stage IA (tumor is 2 centimeters or smaller) and Stage IB (tumor is larger than 2 centimeters but not larger than 4 centimeters).

list.title: Stage II:
list.snippet: Cancer has started to grow outside the pancreas, potentially into nearby tissues and lymph nodes, but not into distant organs.

list.title: Stage III:
list.snippet: Cancer has spread to major blood vessels or nerves near the pancreas or into a significant number of nearby lymph nodes.

list.title: Stage IV (Metastatic):
list.snippet: Cancer has spread to distant organs like the liver, lungs, or peritoneum.
